from.place: The proof clause invoking Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma 20.26.9 (Stacks Tag 06YD): the stalk of each flat sheaf module is a flat module.

title: Stalks of flat sheaves are flat modules
statement: Let (X,\mathcal O_X) be a ringed space and let \mathcal F be a flat \mathcal O_X-module sheaf [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], meaning that tensoring with \mathcal F preserves short exact sequences of \mathcal O_X-modules. For every point x of X, the stalk \mathcal F_x is a flat module over the stalk ring \mathcal O_{X,x}, meaning that tensoring with \mathcal F_x preserves exact sequences of \mathcal O_{X,x}-modules.

proof.text: Fix a point $x$ and an injective linear map $f:M\to N$ of stalk modules. The skyscraper functor [def-pc-ringed-module-skyscraper] sends it to a monomorphism: its maps on sections are pointwise $f$, so cancellation holds at each membership proof.

proof.text: Flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] supplies preservation of finite limits by right tensoring with $\mathcal F$. Consequently the skyscraper map tensored with $\mathcal F$ is monic. Package this as exactness of a short complex whose first map is zero.

source.place: Tag 05NE, lemma-flat-stalks-flat, flat sheaf implies flat stalks; injectivity criterion for flatness

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] to this short complex. Its stalk is exact; since the first map is still zero, its second map is monic. Naturality of [lem-pc-ringed-space-module-stalk-tensor] identifies this second map, up to conjugation by isomorphisms, with the skyscraper stalk map tensored with $\mathcal F_x$.

source.place: Tag 05NE, lemma-flat-stalks-flat, flat sheaf implies flat stalks; injectivity criterion for flatness

proof.text: For [def-pc-ringed-module-skyscraper], send a vector to the germ of its constant global section. Every neighbourhood section is a function on a subsingleton inhabited domain and hence constant; equality of germs detects the value, so this map is bijective. Representing scalars locally proves linearity, and [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] takes pointwise maps to their maps on constant germs. These natural linear isomorphisms conjugate the skyscraper stalk map to $f$. Tensoring these isomorphisms preserves them, so $f\otimes\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F_x}$ is monic. Mathlib Module.Flat.iff_rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap concludes flatness.

statement_change.what: For a general ringed space the stalk ring need not be local: on a one-point space with structure ring Z, its unique stalk is Z, which has multiple maximal ideals. Replace only the erroneous adjective local by stalk; no locally ringed hypothesis is added.
